outcome: need for an invasive procedure caused by flow restriction or abdominal pain
invasive procedures (PD catheter tip migration, occlusion of the lumen with fibrin, omental wrapping, adherence to the bowel, development of new adhesions)
cohort: Individuals undergoing laparoscopic peritoneal dialysis (PD) catheter insertion from eight centers in Canada and the United States were prospectively enrolled.
finding: People with intra-Abdominal adhesions undergoing PD catheter insertion were at higher risk for abdominal pain or flow restriction preventing PD from starting, PD termination, or requiring an invasive procedure within 6 months of insertion.
